content.text: Welcome to [ORG_1]. This handbook accompanies you through your first weeks and months with us. It explains how the company is organised, what you can expect on your first day, how working time, pay and benefits work, and whom you can ask when something is unclear. Please read it before your first day and keep it at hand during your probation period. Where a topic is governed by a works agreement or by your employment contract, the agreement or the contract always takes precedence over this handbook.

We are glad that you have decided to join us. [ORG_1] has been building precision measuring instruments for more than seventy years, and the company has always relied on people who take pride in careful work. Our customers in mechanical engineering, the automotive supply chain and medical technology trust our gauges, probes and coordinate measuring systems because every instrument leaves our site calibrated to the micrometre. That level of quality is only possible when every team, from assembly to accounting, works with the same care.

Joining a new employer always means many new names, rules and systems at once. Nobody expects you to know everything after a week. Ask questions, write things down and give yourself time. Your manager, your buddy and the HR team are there to help you settle in, and we would rather answer the same question twice than have you guess.

The handbook is structured along the order in which topics typically become relevant: first the preparation before your start, then your first week, then the rules that apply to your everyday working life. Each section names a contact person. The table of key contacts at the end of the handbook lists email addresses and phone numbers for all central functions. The current version of this handbook is always available on the intranet at
. Printed copies may be outdated, so please check the intranet if you are unsure.

The company was founded in 1953 by [PERSON_3] as a small workshop for dial gauges in [LOCATION_1]. In the 1970s the product range grew to include electronic length measurement, and in 1991 the company moved to its current site at [ADDRESS_1]. Today [ORG_1] employs around 650 people, about 520 of them at the headquarters and the remainder at our service and sales offices in [LOCATION_2] and [LOCATION_3]. The company is still owned by the founding family and is managed in the third generation by [PERSON_4].

Being family-owned shapes how we work. We plan for the long term, we reinvest most of our profits into research, equipment and training, and we try to make decisions close to the people who have to live with them. Many colleagues have been with the company for twenty or thirty years, and we are proud that a large share of our managers started as apprentices on our own shop floor.
Our product range is divided into three business units:
: dial gauges, bore gauges, height gauges and digital calipers for workshops and inspection rooms
: inline probes, air gauging stations and multi-point measuring fixtures that are integrated into our customers' production lines
: an accredited calibration laboratory, on-site service and training for customers
Around 60 percent of our revenue is generated outside Germany. Our largest markets are the European Union, the United States and China, where we work with long-standing distribution partners.
Four values guide how we work together and how we treat our customers:
: we measure twice, document what we do and do not accept "roughly right" when exactness is required.
: we keep our promises to customers and to each other, and we say early when a deadline is at risk.
: we treat every colleague fairly, regardless of position, origin, gender, age, religion or sexual orientation.
: we question routines, learn from mistakes and share what we know.

To set up your personnel file, your payroll and your IT access in time, HR needs a few documents from you. Please send them to [EMAIL_1] or bring them along on your first day at the latest. Without these documents we cannot pay your first salary on time.
Signed employment contract and signed data protection information
Tax identification number and, if applicable, information on your church tax status
Social security number or your social security card
Name of your statutory health insurance fund or proof of private health insurance
Bank details for salary payments: [IBAN_1], or the IBAN of another account in your own name
Certificates and qualifications relevant to your position
For positions in the calibration laboratory: proof of your training on measurement uncertainty, if available
For employees who are not EU citizens: residence and work permit
Use this checklist in the days before you start:
Confirm your start date and starting time with HR
Check that you have received the welcome email with your parking permit and the site plan
Read this handbook and the house rules on the intranet
Plan your route: the site can be reached by the regional train to [LOCATION_1] station and the shuttle bus, or by car via the north gate
Bring safety shoes if you already own a pair that meets class S3; otherwise we will provide them
Bring your personal documents listed above
Prepare any questions you would like to discuss with your manager in the first week

Before your first day, your manager and the IT team prepare your workstation, your user account, your email address and, depending on your position, your laptop, mobile phone and access card. Your manager also selects a buddy for you, an experienced colleague from your team or a neighbouring team who is not your superior. You will receive your buddy's name in the welcome email.

Your first week is planned in detail so that you get to know the people, the processes and the site step by step. The exact programme depends on your department; the following schedule shows a typical first week for employees in administration and engineering. Employees in production follow a schedule that includes additional safety training and a longer introduction at their workstation.
Welcome at reception, issue of access card and parking permit
Welcome breakfast and introduction to the company
IT handover: laptop, accounts, password and multi-factor authentication
Tour of the site including production and calibration laboratory
First meeting with your manager: tasks, goals and contacts
General occupational safety and fire protection briefing
Introduction to the quality management system
Introduction to time recording and the employee self-service portal
Data protection and information security training
Job shadowing in your own team
Introduction to the ERP system for your role
Review of the first week with your manager
Lunch with your team in the staff restaurant

On the first day please report to reception at the main entrance at 08:30. Reception will issue your access card and accompany you to the welcome breakfast. If you are delayed, please call reception at [PHONE_1].
Your First Days at Your Workstation

From the second week onwards, the focus shifts to your actual tasks. Your manager agrees an individual induction plan with you that lists the topics, systems and processes you need to learn in your first three months. The plan names a responsible colleague for each topic and a target date. Please keep the plan up to date and bring it to your feedback meetings.

The regular working time at [ORG_1] is 37.5 hours per week for full-time employees, distributed over five working days from Monday to Friday. Part-time arrangements are agreed individually in the employment contract. In production, work is organised in two or three shifts; the shift schedules are published four weeks in advance on the notice boards and in the employee self-service portal.

All employees record their working time electronically. You clock in and out at the terminals at the entrances or, if you work in administration, via the time recording app on your computer. Breaks of at least 30 minutes for working days of more than six hours and 45 minutes for working days of more than nine hours are deducted automatically in accordance with the Working Hours Act.

Employees outside shift operations work in a flexitime model. The flexible working window runs from 06:30 to 19:00. The core working time from 09:00 to 15:00 on Mondays to Thursdays and from 09:00 to 12:00 on Fridays applies to all employees in flexitime; during core time you should be available unless you have agreed otherwise with your manager. Your time account may show a balance of up to plus 60 hours or minus 20 hours. If your balance exceeds plus 40 hours, please agree with your manager how to reduce it.

Overtime is work that your manager has ordered in advance and that exceeds your contractual working hours. Hours that you work voluntarily within flexitime are not overtime. Ordered overtime is first credited to your time account. If a reduction through time off is not possible within six months for operational reasons, it is paid out with a supplement of 25 percent. Details are set out in the works agreement on working time, which you can find on

Full-time employees are entitled to 30 working days of paid holiday per calendar year. In addition, 24 and 31 December are days off at the company. Holiday requests are submitted via the employee self-service portal and approved by your manager. Please plan your holiday early and coordinate it with your team. In the first six months of employment you acquire your holiday entitlement proportionately; in justified cases your manager can approve holiday earlier.

The company closes for two weeks in August and for the period between Christmas and New Year. The exact dates are announced in January each year. Employees who are needed for maintenance work or customer service during the closure are informed by their manager by the end of March.

If you are unable to work due to illness, please inform your manager before the start of your working time on the first day, by phone or by message. From the fourth calendar day of illness, a medical certificate is required. Doctors now transmit certificates electronically to your health insurance fund; HR retrieves them from there. You only need to inform us that you are ill and how long you expect to be absent. Other absences, such as medical appointments or official appointments, should be scheduled outside core time where possible.

Your salary is paid monthly in arrears and is credited to your account on the last working day of the month. Your payslip is available in the employee self-service portal from the 25th of each month. [ORG_1] is not bound by a collective agreement, but the company follows the structure of the regional metalworking agreement for its pay grades and reviews salaries once a year in April. If you have questions about your payslip, please contact payroll at [EMAIL_2].
In addition to the monthly salary, the company pays:
A holiday bonus amounting to 50 percent of a monthly salary, paid with the June salary
A Christmas bonus amounting to 55 percent of a monthly salary, paid with the November salary
A profit-sharing bonus, which depends on the annual result and is decided by the management each spring
We offer a range of benefits. Some are available from your first day, others after the end of your probation period:
Company pension scheme with an employer contribution of 20 percent on deferred compensation
Group accident insurance that also covers leisure time
Occupational disability insurance at a reduced group rate
Subsidised public transport ticket for the regional network
Free charging stations for electric cars and bicycles in the staff car park
Annual health day with check-ups by the company doctor
Subsidised membership in partner fitness studios
Childcare allowance for children who are not yet of school age
Subsidised lunch in the staff restaurant
Free water, coffee and tea at all workplaces
Further details and application forms can be found on

On your first day you will receive your user account, your email address and, depending on your role, a laptop and a mobile phone. You will set your own password during the IT handover. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all accounts; you will need the authenticator app on your company phone or, if you do not have one, a hardware token from the IT service desk.
The IT security policy applies to all employees. Its most important rules are:
Never share your password, not even with the IT service desk
Lock your screen whenever you leave your workstation
Store business documents only on the network drives or in the document management system, not on local drives or private storage
Do not install software yourself; request it via the IT self-service portal
Report suspicious emails immediately using the report button in your email client
Use private devices for company data only if they are registered in the device management system

The IT service desk is available from 07:00 to 17:00 on working days at [PHONE_2] and [EMAIL_3]. Outside these hours, an on-call service is available for production systems only. Most standard requests, such as a new monitor, a software installation or access to a shared folder, can be submitted via

The site at [ADDRESS_1] has two entrances. The main entrance with reception is on the south side and is open from 06:00 to 20:00. The north gate is used by delivery traffic and by employees in shift operations and can be opened at any time with your access card. The staff car park has around 480 spaces, including 24 charging spaces for electric cars and a covered bicycle shelter with lockers. Parking is free of charge, but you need the parking permit that you received with your welcome email. Visitors park in the marked spaces in front of reception.

The company shuttle bus runs between [LOCATION_1] station and the main entrance every 20 minutes in the morning between 05:20 and 08:40 and in the afternoon between 14:00 and 18:20. The timetable is aligned with the regional trains and is adjusted twice a year when the train timetable changes. If you use public transport, ask HR about the subsidised ticket described in the section on benefits.

Our staff restaurant in building C serves breakfast from 07:00 to 09:30 and lunch from 11:30 to 13:45. Every day there is a choice of three dishes, one of them vegetarian, as well as a salad bar. Meals are paid for with your access card; the subsidy of the company is deducted automatically. Employees in the late shift can buy snacks and hot meals from the vending area next to the restaurant, which is open around the clock. Each building also has kitchenettes with refrigerators and coffee machines that all teams share. Please leave them as you would like to find them.

There is no general dress code in the offices. Most colleagues dress casually; for customer visits and trade fairs, business attire is expected. In production, in the warehouse and in the calibration laboratory, workwear and personal protective equipment are mandatory. The company provides workwear, safety shoes and safety glasses free of charge and has the workwear cleaned weekly. In the calibration laboratory, additional rules apply to reduce dust and temperature fluctuations; you will be instructed accordingly if you work there.

All visitors must register at reception, where they receive a visitor badge and a short safety briefing. Visitors may only enter production areas when accompanied by an employee. If you are expecting a visitor, please register them in advance in the visitor management system so that reception can prepare the badge. Private parcels cannot be delivered to the site.

Important news from the management, from HR and from the works council is published on the intranet. Production employees without a computer workstation receive the same information via the notice boards in the halls and via the employee app, which you can install on your private phone on a voluntary basis. Once a quarter, the management holds a company meeting in the staff restaurant, which is also streamed to the sales offices. At these meetings, the management reports on business development, major projects and investments and answers questions from employees.

Our working language at the site is German, but many teams work with international customers and partners, and an increasing number of colleagues do not speak German as their first language. Documents for customers and for the international sales network are written in English. Internal meetings are held in German unless at least one participant does not speak it; in that case we switch to English. If you would like to improve your German or English, the company offers language courses during working time.
For daily collaboration we use the following tools:
The email and calendar system for appointments and external correspondence
The team chat for quick questions and coordination within and between teams
The document management system for all controlled documents, such as work instructions, test plans and drawings
The ERP system for orders, materials, production planning and invoicing
The ticket system for requests to IT, facility management and the maintenance team

Please use the team chat for informal questions and keep important agreements in email or in the relevant system so that they can be traced later. Customer data and technical drawings must never be shared via private messaging services.

As an employee you will have access to confidential information, such as customer orders, drawings, prices and personal data of colleagues and customers. Your employment contract contains a confidentiality clause that continues to apply after you leave the company. In practice this means that you discuss confidential information only with colleagues who need it for their work, that you do not leave documents lying around on printers or desks, and that you do not take business documents home in paper form without your manager's approval.

The processing of personal data is subject to the GDPR and the Federal Data Protection Act. You will receive a separate data protection training in your first week. If you are unsure whether you may use or pass on certain data, ask the data protection coordinator [PERSON_7] before you act. Data protection incidents, for example an email sent to the wrong recipient or a lost laptop, must be reported immediately to [EMAIL_6] so that the company can meet its legal reporting deadlines.

Occupational safety has the highest priority at [ORG_1]. Many of our workstations involve machines, compressed air, solvents or heavy loads. Even in the offices, the most common causes of accidents are tripping, falling and carrying. You will receive a general safety briefing in your first week and a briefing specific to your workstation from your manager. Both briefings are repeated once a year.
Please observe the following rules at all times:
Wear the personal protective equipment prescribed for your area, in particular safety shoes and safety glasses in production.
Use only the marked footpaths in the production halls and never walk through forklift lanes.
Operate machines only after you have been instructed and authorised to do so.
Never remove or bypass protective devices on machines.
Keep escape routes, fire extinguishers and emergency exits free at all times.
Report every accident, however minor, to your manager and have it recorded in the first-aid book.
Report near misses and hazards so that we can eliminate them before anyone is hurt.

In an emergency, call the internal emergency number 112 from any company phone; the call is forwarded to the fire brigade and simultaneously to the plant security. First aiders are marked on the notice boards in every building. Assembly points for evacuations are shown on the escape route plans. Please familiarise yourself with the nearest escape route and assembly point during your first week.

The company doctor holds consultation hours at the site every Tuesday and Thursday. Consultations are confidential and take place during working time. Employees in certain areas, such as the paint shop or the calibration laboratory, attend mandatory occupational health check-ups; HR will invite you if this applies to you.

Your buddy is an experienced colleague who helps you find your way around in the first months. Your buddy shows you the site, introduces you to colleagues in other departments, explains unwritten rules and is your first point of contact for all the questions you might hesitate to ask your manager. We recommend that you meet your buddy at least once a week in the first month and every two weeks after that. The buddy programme officially ends after six months, but many buddy pairs stay in contact far longer.
During your probation period you will have three structured feedback meetings with your manager:
: first impressions, open questions and the status of your induction plan
: performance and development so far, goals for the remaining probation period
Before the end of the probation period
: overall assessment and decision on the continuation of your employment

The meetings are documented on a short form that you and your manager sign. If you have the impression that something is not going well, please do not wait for the next scheduled meeting; talk to your manager, your buddy or HR at any time.

The probation period is six months unless your contract states otherwise. During this time, either party may terminate the employment relationship with two weeks' notice. Your manager will inform you of the result of the final assessment at least four weeks before the probation period ends. After the probation period you become eligible for the full range of benefits and for internal training programmes.

[ORG_1] has an elected works council with eleven members, chaired by [PERSON_2]. The works council represents the interests of all employees under the Works Constitution Act and has co-determination rights in many areas, such as working time, the introduction of technical systems and the principles of remuneration. The works council office is located in building B, first floor, and holds consultation hours every Wednesday from 13:00 to 15:00. You can contact the works council at [EMAIL_4].

In addition, there is a representative body for severely disabled employees and a youth and apprentice representation. Employees with a severe disability or an equivalent status can contact [PERSON_8], who represents their interests confidentially.

The company invests in the development of its employees because our products and processes change constantly. Every employee is entitled to at least three days of further training per year. Training needs are discussed in the annual employee review, which takes place between October and December. Internal courses on measurement technology, quality methods, languages and software are published in the training catalogue on
. External training is approved by your manager and HR and is generally paid by the company.

For employees who want to take on more responsibility, [ORG_1] offers a two-year development programme for future team leaders and supports part-time studies, for example in mechanical engineering or business administration, with a share of the tuition fees and paid study days.
When will I receive my first salary?

Your first salary is paid on the last working day of your first full month, provided that HR has received all the documents listed in the section on preparation. If you start in the second half of a month, your first salary may be paid together with the salary for the following month.

Employees in administration and engineering can work from home on up to two days per week once they have completed their first three months, provided that their tasks allow it and their manager agrees. The details are regulated in the works agreement on mobile work. During the induction phase we ask you to work on site so that you can get to know your colleagues and processes.
What happens if I forget my access card?

Reception can issue a day card for you after checking your identity. Please note that the day card does not allow you to record your working time; ask your manager to correct your time account in the portal afterwards.
Whom do I ask if I do not know whom to ask?

Your buddy is always the right first contact. If your buddy cannot help, HR will find the right person for you. There is no question that is too small, and nobody at the company will think less of you for asking.
How can I give feedback on my onboarding?

After three months you will receive a short anonymous survey on your onboarding experience. The results are evaluated by HR together with the works council and are used to improve the programme for future colleagues. Of course, you can also give feedback at any time in person or by email to [EMAIL_1].
May I take part in sports and social activities?

Yes, and we encourage it. The company supports a running group, a football team, a choir and a cycling club, all organised by employees. Information and contact persons can be found on the intranet. Every summer, the company invites all employees and their families to a summer party on the site, and in December there is a Christmas party for each department.
The following table lists the most important contacts for new employees. Your manager and your buddy are not listed because you will receive their details in your welcome email.
We wish you a good start at [ORG_1] and look forward to working with you. If you have suggestions for improving this handbook, please send them to [EMAIL_1].
